seo.title: Factors of 20 Math Clicker - Division & Divisibility Practice
seo.metaDescription: Spot all 6 factors of 20 on a 10x10 math grid. Fast-paced factor pair identification for elementary and middle school students.
seo.intro: Twenty is a composite number with 6 factors: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, and 20. Its factor pairs are 1 x 20, 2 x 10, and 4 x 5. Locating these factors on a 100-number board strengthens connections between fives, tens, and evens, laying essential groundwork for percentage benchmarks (like 5%, 10%, 20%, 25%, and 50%). Fluency Development: When students engage in timed identification on a 100-number grid, they move beyond manual finger-counting and transition into visual pattern synthesis. Developing automaticity with this specific math concept reduces cognitive load during multi-step problem solving, long division, and algebraic equation manipulation.
seo.howToPlay: Click all 6 factors of 20 on the 100-tile grid. Correct tiles turn green with a checkmark. Incorrect clicks flash red and deduct 2 seconds from your round clock. Locate all 6 factors before time runs out. Keyboard and Accessibility Controls: Students can use a touchscreen, trackpad, mouse, or keyboard arrow keys to navigate between tiles. Pressing Space or Enter activates the focused tile. Wrong clicks temporarily flash red with an X icon and subtract 2 seconds, but remain unlocked so learners can self-correct without getting stuck.
seo.teacherNotes: Connect the factors of 20 to money and coins: 1 cent (pennies), 2 cents, 5 cents (nickels), 10 cents (dimes), and 20 cents. Classroom Implementation Ideas: Use this interactive grid during the first five minutes of math instruction as an energetic bell-ringer or daily warm-up. Teachers can project the screen onto an interactive whiteboard for whole-class competitive rounds, or assign the canonical link directly into Google Classroom for independent Chromebook math station rotations.

faq.q: What are all the factors of 20?
How does mastering click all factors of 20 support higher-level math standards?
faq.a: Building speed and accuracy with click all factors of 20 directly strengthens mental arithmetic and numerical reasoning. When foundational number facts become second nature, students can dedicate their active working memory to advanced problem-solving strategies, fraction equivalence, and multi-step word problems.
